chapters.title: Chapter 1: Why Valuation Matters to You

lessons.title: Where Valuation Shows Up at Work: Fundraises, ESOPs, Acquisitions and Buybacks

children.text: Sahyadri Foods Private Limited is a fictional Nashik company selling ready-to-cook meals. Over eighteen months it raises a round, grants employee options, is approached by a listed FMCG group, and argues with its auditor about the value of a business it bought two years earlier. Four completely different teams handle those four events. All four are valuation events, and in each one somebody has to defend a number.

body.text: Valuation is not an annual ritual for the finance team. It is a gate the company passes through every time shares change hands, options are granted, a business is bought or sold, or cash is returned to shareholders.

children.text: The Five Moments Valuation Lands on Someone's Desk

cells: Raising money
To fix the price per share at which new shares are issued
Negotiated between founders and investors, supported by a valuer where the law requires one
How much of the company the investor gets
Granting or exercising ESOPs
To set the exercise price and, at exercise, the taxable perquisite value
A SEBI-registered Category I merchant banker for unlisted shares
What employees pay, and what tax they owe
Buying or selling a business
To set an offer price and then a final purchase price after diligence
Buyer and seller teams, with transaction advisers and valuers
Whether the deal happens and on what terms
Buying back shares
To fix the buyback price and to justify using cash this way
The board, advised on price and on the legal limits
What shareholders are paid to exit
Reporting and compliance
To test acquired goodwill for impairment, price share transfers and meet FEMA or tax rules
Auditors, registered valuers and merchant bankers
What the accounts show and whether filings stand up

children.text: 1. Fundraising: The Number in the Term Sheet
Every funding round turns on two figures.
Pre-money valuation
is what the company is agreed to be worth before the new money arrives.
Post-money valuation
is that figure plus the investment itself. The investor's stake comes off the second one, not the first.

markDefs.definition: The agreed value of the company before the new investment comes in.
Pre-money valuation plus the new investment. The investor's percentage is calculated on this figure.

body.caption: The denominator is the post-money valuation

children.text: Sahyadri raises ₹40 crore at a pre-money valuation of ₹160 crore. Post-money is ₹200 crore, so the investor holds ₹40 crore ÷ ₹200 crore = 20%, and the founders keep 80%.

body.title: Sahyadri Foods ownership after the round (%)
Work out the stake
body.prompt: A founder agrees to raise ₹25 crore at a pre-money valuation of ₹100 crore. What percentage of the company does the investor end up owning?
body.explanation: Post-money is ₹100 crore + ₹25 crore = ₹125 crore. The investor holds ₹25 crore ÷ ₹125 crore = 20%. Confuse pre and post, and you will quote 25% by mistake, which is a ₹5 crore error in the founder's favour that no investor will let pass.

children.text: Listing on the exchange is the same negotiation at a larger scale, with the public as the investor and far more scrutiny of the multiple.

body.label: Lenskart IPO, November 2025
body.context: The eyewear company listed at a valuation of roughly ₹70,000 crore against an FY25 profit of about ₹297 crore, which works out to around 235 times earnings. Analysts argued loudly about that multiple, the issue was still subscribed about 28 times, and the stock listed close to 3% below the issue price.

body.text: Notice what the Lenskart argument was not about. Nobody disputed the revenue or the profit. The entire fight was over the multiple applied to them, which is another way of saying the fight was over future growth and risk.

children.text: 2. ESOPs: Two Valuations, Two Different Purposes
Employee options involve the same share being valued twice, for different reasons, at different dates. HR teams field the questions both times.

body.caption: The two valuation moments in an ESOP

cells: Grant
The exercise price set for the option, usually linked to a recent valuation
The board, guided by a valuation report
It fixes what the employee will pay years later
Exercise
The fair market value of the share on the exercise date
A SEBI-registered Category I merchant banker, for unlisted shares
The gap over the exercise price is taxed as salary perquisite
Sale or buyback
The price actually received for the share
The buyer, or the company in a buyback
Capital gains are computed from the fair market value already taxed

children.text: The tax rule sits in the salary provisions, not the capital gains ones. The excess of fair market value on the exercise date over what the employee paid is a perquisite under Section 17(1)(d) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 [Section 17(2)(vi) of the Income-tax Act, 1961], with the valuation mechanics in Section 17(5)(h).

body.title: The tax bill nobody warned them about
body.prompt: Priya exercises 5,000 vested options in an unlisted company at an exercise price of ₹50 per share. The merchant banker's report puts fair market value at ₹300 per share on the exercise date. What is the perquisite value added to her salary income, in ₹?
body.explanation: 5,000 × (₹300 - ₹50) = 5,000 × ₹250 = ₹12,50,000. That amount is taxed at her slab rate as salary, even though she has not sold a single share and may not be able to for years.

body.text: This is the most common ESOP shock in Indian startups: real tax on paper gains, payable in cash, on shares with no market. Employees of eligible startups can defer the tax deduction on this perquisite under Section 392(3) read with Section 289(3) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 [Section 192(1C) of the Income-tax Act, 1961], but the relief is narrow and the conditions are strict.

children.text: 3. Buying or Selling a Business
In a deal, valuation is not one event. The number is set, tested, adjusted and then revisited for years afterwards in the accounts.

body.title: How a valuation number travels through one deal

events.title: Indicative offer
events.description: The buyer applies a multiple to reported EBITDA and offers a range, subject to diligence. Nothing is committed yet.

events.title: Due diligence rebuilds the numbers
events.description: One-off income is stripped out, promoter expenses are added back, and a normalised EBITDA emerges. This number, not the reported one, drives the price.

events.title: Binding offer and the bridge to equity value
events.description: Enterprise value is converted into what the seller actually receives, after deducting debt and adjusting for cash and working capital. Lesson 3.2 covers this bridge.

events.title: Price allocated across what was bought
events.description: The accounting team splits the price across brands, customer relationships and other assets, with the remainder recorded as goodwill.

events.title: Impairment testing
events.description: The acquired business is revalued annually. If it is worth less than the amount carried in the books, the difference is written off through the profit and loss account.

body.text: Impairment is where optimistic deal valuations come back to the same management team years later. A write-off is an admission, in audited accounts, that the business is worth less than what was paid for it.

children.text: 4. Buybacks: Paying Cash to Shrink

When a company buys back its own shares, the board is making a valuation statement with real money: that the company's own shares are a better use of cash than anything else available. In a tender offer, the price is set above the market price to persuade shareholders to participate.

body.caption: Three Indian buyback prices against the market
headers: Premium to the market price at announcement

cells: Infosys, September 2025
₹1,800 per share, about ₹18,000 crore in total
About 19% above the previous close
Wipro, October 2020
₹400 per share, about ₹9,500 crore in total
About 6% above the previous close
BHEL, October 2018
₹86 per share, about ₹1,628 crore in total
About 28% above the then market price of roughly ₹67

body.title: What a buyback price signals
body.question: A board approves a tender offer buyback at ₹1,800 when the stock trades around ₹1,512. Which reading of that decision is the most defensible?
options: The board is guaranteeing the share price will reach ₹1,800 and stay there
The board believes the shares are worth at least ₹1,800 and that returning cash beats the alternative uses of it
The premium proves the market price was manipulated
A buyback always increases the value of the company
body.explanation: A buyback at a premium says two things at once: management thinks the shares are worth paying up for, and it has no better internal project for that cash. It guarantees nothing about the future price. A buyback funded at too high a price destroys value for the shareholders who stay.

children.text: Tax treatment of the money you receive has changed repeatedly. Buyback proceeds received on or after 1 April 2026 are taxed as capital gains in the shareholder's hands under the Income-tax Act, 2025, with the cost of acquisition allowed as a deduction (Section 69 read with Section 2(40)(f)). Between 1 October 2024 and 31 March 2026 the same receipts were treated as deemed dividend under Section 2(22)(f) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, with no cost deduction at all. Check the position on the day you tender, not the one you remember.
5. The Valuations You Never See
Most valuation work never makes the news. It sits inside compliance files, and it is usually where a manager first meets a registered valuer.

body.title: Common valuations the law or the accounts demand

children.text: Issuing shares for consideration other than cash, or to a non-resident investor under FEMA pricing rules
Transferring unlisted shares between shareholders, where income tax rules prescribe a valuation method
Schemes of merger, demerger or arrangement placed before the National Company Law Tribunal
Annual impairment testing of goodwill and of investments in subsidiaries
Valuation of a corporate debtor during insolvency proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

The Companies Act, 2013 requires many of these to be carried out by a registered valuer. Lesson 5.1 covers who qualifies and Lesson 5.2 covers the specific rules for fundraises, ESOPs and share transfers.

body.title: The stale valuation report
body.scenario: You head HR at an unlisted Hyderabad software company. The board wants to grant ESOPs to 40 new employees next month. The most recent merchant banker's valuation report is 14 months old and values the shares at ₹210. A Series C round is expected to close in about three months at a price everyone privately expects to be far higher. The CFO suggests granting at ₹210 because "the report is on file".
body.prompt: What issues would you raise before the grant goes ahead?
body.modelAnswer:
1. Age of the report. A 14 month old valuation reflects a company that has since grown and is about to raise at a higher price. Ask whether a fresh report is needed for the grant to stand up later.
2. Purpose of the report. Check what that report was prepared for. A valuation done for a different purpose may not support an ESOP grant.
3. What the employees are actually promised. A low exercise price sounds generous, but the perquisite tax at exercise is calculated on the gap to fair market value on that future date. A lower exercise price means a larger taxable perquisite later.
4. Timing against the round. Granting weeks before a round closes at a much higher price invites questions from auditors, investors and the tax authorities. Either grant now with a defensible current valuation, or wait.
5. Communication. Employees need to understand that the grant price is not the value of their shares, that exercise triggers tax in cash, and that liquidity depends on a buyback or an exit.
6. Documentation. Board resolution, the valuation report it relies on, the ESOP scheme terms and the grant letters must all name the same price and date.

body.title: Complete the equation
body.textWithBlank: Post-money valuation equals pre-money valuation plus the amount ___.
body.explanation: Post-money = pre-money + new investment. The investor's percentage is always calculated on the post-money figure.

body.title: Your valuation calendar for the year
steps: List every event in the next 12 months that will need a valuation: rounds, grants, transfers, deals, buybacks
For each one, note who is required to produce the valuation and under which rulebook
Check the date of the most recent valuation report on file and what purpose it was prepared for
Identify which events need a fresh report rather than a reused one
Agree who briefs employees or shareholders on what the number does and does not mean
Diary the annual impairment test for any business the company has acquired

body.label: Chittorgarh: live and past buyback offers in India
body.description: Track tender offer buybacks with their offer prices and dates. Compare each buyback price against where the stock was trading when the board approved it.

cards.definition: The agreed value of a company before new investment comes in.
Pre-money valuation plus the new investment. The investor's stake is calculated on this.
The fixed amount an employee pays per share when exercising an option.
The excess of fair market value on the exercise date over the exercise price, taxed as salary.
Reported EBITDA adjusted for one-off and non-business items, used as the base for a deal multiple.
A write-off recorded when an acquired business is worth less than the amount carried in the books.
A company offering to repurchase its own shares at a fixed price, usually above the market price.

points: Valuation shows up at five recurring moments: fundraises, ESOPs, deals, buybacks and reporting or compliance.
In a fundraise, the investor's stake is investment divided by post-money valuation. ₹40 crore into a ₹160 crore pre-money company buys 20%, not 25%.
ESOPs are valued twice. The exercise price is set at grant, and the fair market value at exercise creates a real cash tax bill on a paper gain.
A deal valuation is tested at diligence, adjusted in the bridge from enterprise value to equity value, and revisited annually through impairment testing.
A buyback price set above the market, such as Infosys at ₹1,800 in September 2025, is a board making a public statement about value.
Most valuation work is compliance driven and never makes the news, but it is the work most likely to land on a manager's desk.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment, tax or legal advice. Sahyadri Foods and the companies in the exercises are fictional. Real company figures are from public reports at the time of the events described. Tax provisions are cited in outline and change often, including through annual Finance Acts. Confirm the current position with a qualified professional before acting.
